draft.title: Rural, remote and low-income groups
card: On average, people in rural and remote areas and people on low incomes have poorer health than other Australians. This is a pattern across groups, not a rule for every person.
Distance
People outside major cities often live far from GPs, specialists and hospitals. Travel takes time and money, and fewer services are available, so care can be delayed.
Cost
Low-income households may struggle to pay for medicines, dental care, healthy food or travel to appointments. Some then put off seeing a health professional.
Risk factors
Rates of risk factors such as smoking and inactivity can be higher in these groups. Limited access to services makes these risks harder to reduce.
draft.remember: Distance, cost and risk factors combine to make access to care harder and health poorer on average.

a.q: Which statement best explains why people in remote areas tend to have poorer health on average?
opts: Services are far away, so care can be delayed
Remote residents choose not to value their health
Remote areas have no health risk factors at all
Everyone in remote areas has a low income
a.why: Distance from GPs, specialists and hospitals makes care harder to reach, so problems may be treated late. It is wrong to say people do not value their health, because the barrier is access, not attitude.
a.clue: Think about how far people must travel to reach care.

b.q: Dean earns a low income in a large city and has toothache. He avoids the dentist for months. Which factor best explains his delay?
opts: The cost of dental care is hard for his budget
The nearest dentist is hundreds of kilometres away
He lives in a remote area with few services
He has a high rate of smoking and inactivity
b.why: Dean lives in a city, so the barrier is the cost of care on a low income. Distance is a tempting answer, but it does not fit a person living in a large city.
b.clue: Check where Dean lives and what his income is.

a.best: Services are far away, so care can be delayed

b.best: The cost of dental care is hard for his budget

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about how far people must travel to reach care' points straight to the distance option, so it gives the answer away.
The three distractors are absurd ('choose not to value their health', 'everyone has a low income', 'no health risk factors at all'), so a Year 12 student can pick the answer without knowing the idea.

The remember line says risk factors combine with distance and cost to make access to care harder. The card says the reverse: limited access makes risk factors harder to reduce. Risk factors do not themselves make access harder.

a.q: Which statement about health in remote areas is accurate?
opts: Health is poorer on average, partly due to distance
Every remote resident has poorer health than city people
Health is poorer only because smoking rates are higher
Higher risk factors make health services harder to reach
a.why: Poorer health in remote areas is an average pattern, and distance from services is one cause. Saying risk factors make services harder to reach reverses the link: limited access makes risk factors harder to reduce. The other options turn a pattern into a rule or ignore distance and cost.
a.clue: Check which way cause and effect run, and how strong each claim is.
